# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - Gold, silver and platinum traded mainly in response to newsflow last week as all eyes focussed on the ECB summit. A spectacular crash on Thursday saw prices plummet as headlines began to emerge that ECB chief Mario Draghi would not countenance Eurozone bond purchases. By Friday, all bets were off as news that British Prime Minister David Cameron had vetoed a proposed EU treaty change left a cloud of doubt surrounding the long-term consequences of the summit. • Palladium followed its own path, however, and was the only one of the major precious metals to post gains last week. Investors that had begun the week short palladium were doubtless driven to cover after prices held above $630 on Monday and into Tuesday. In addition, an accumulation of option interest at key levels helped maintain buying above $660. - The SPDR Gold Trust—the largest gold ETF by holdings—was a seller last week, shedding more than 81,000 ounces. Total gold ETF holdings nonetheless increased for the ninth consecutive week, and now exceed 70.4 million ounces. Platinum and palladium ETF flows were very subdued, following heavy liquidation in the previous week. • Net long speculative gold positions on COMEX increased for the second consecutive week, up more than 1.1 million ounces to 22.6 million ounces in total. Yet again, we saw a broadly positive correlation with risk sentiment; gold has still yet to rediscover the safe-haven appeal that was so instrumental in driving the great gains made in the summer. Having begun the week above $1,750, gold was sold down almost to $1,700 by Tuesday. As optimism increased towards the beginning of the summit, gold recovered steadily towards the week’s opening level. A spectacular crash on Thursday, however, saw prices drop $50 in no time at all as headlines began to emerge that ECB chief Mario Draghi would not countenance Eurozone bond purchases. By Friday, all bets were off as news that British Prime Minister David Cameron had vetoed a proposed EU treaty change left a cloud of doubt surrounding the long-term consequences of the summit. Gold traded in a jittery $20 range, with most investors reluctant to commit either way given the prevailing uncertainty over the Eurozone’s next moves. - Net long speculative positions on COMEX increased for the second consecutive week, up more than 1.1 million ounces to 22.6 million ounces in total. Increases were especially notable in large speculative options positions, which rose by more than 16%. Liquidation of TOCOM positions accelerated this week, with declines of 248,000 ounces dwarfing the previous week’s decline of 9,700 ounces. - The SPDR Gold Trust—the largest gold ETF by holdings—was a seller last week, shedding more than 81,000 ounces. Total gold ETF holdings nonetheless increased for the ninth consecutive week, and now exceed 70.4 million ounces. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—December 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

||||||| |**Date**|**iShares**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Total**|| |**02-Dec-11**|311,944,660|80,017,410|28,300,463|23,434,618|15,890,859|**459,588,010**|| |**09-Dec-11**|314,084,400|80,116,127|28,338,361|19,759,372|15,890,859|**458,189,119**|| |**Change**|**2,139,740**|**98,717**|**37,898**|**-3,675,246**|**0**|**-1,398,891**|| - Silver moved largely in tandem with gold last week, vulnerable to the same headline-driven moves as the yellow metal. Thursday’s liquidation was felt more acutely in silver: with spot having been bid as high as $33.24, the subsequent sweep down to $31.40 represented a drop of nearly 5.9%. From this low, prices recovered on Friday to end the week above $32.00—barely a dollar lower than where they had started on Monday. - Net long speculative positions in silver increased by 8.8 million ounces in the first week of December—a strong rebound in favour of long interest after the net shortening that was seen at the end of November. This reversal was driven by an impressive increase in small speculative futures positions, which alone accounted for more than 6.4 million ounces of the total increase. Large speculative options positions remain healthy, despite a small reduction last week. - Most of the major silver ETFs added to their holdings last week. However, these were more than offset by liquidation of more nearly 3.7 million ounces from the US ETFS fund. Overall silver ETF holdings decreased by 1.4 million ounces; following the previous week’s addition of 2.8 million ounces, we see that silver ETF flows are as prone to fluctuations as the price of the metal itself. #### **Silver Exchange Investment, April 09—December 11** 450 50 Silver price, $/oz

Spot platinum made lows around $1,487 on Friday, down from almost $1,560 on Monday. A late rally leading to an endof-week close at $1,515 could hardly disguise the fact that it had been a poor week for platinum. The declines continued a downtrend extending back to mid-November, and the break below $1,500 at the end of the week marked the first breach of this level since mid-October. - The platinum futures markets experienced another relatively quiet week, with very little to report on NYMEX. Liquidation amounting to 50,000 ounces on TOCOM was evidence of heightened bearishness towards platinum. - After shedding more than 70,000 ounces in the last week of November, platinum ETFs were largely inactive last week, their selling energy spent for the moment. Relative stasis could persist as long as platinum remains between $1,500$1,550; expect activity to recommence if we see a breakout either side of this zone. #### **Platinum Exchange Investment Apr 09—December 11** 2,500 2,000

||||||| |**Date**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Other**|**Total**|| |**02-Dec-11**|402,837|473,462|635,223|130,893|154,194|**1,796,609**|| |**09-Dec-11**|396,555|468,400|634,468|130,893|154,193|**1,784,509**|| |**Change**|**-6,282**|**-5,062**|**-755**|**0**|**-1**|**-12,100**|| - In contrast to the other three major precious metals, palladium made solid gains last week, ending Friday above $680, up $40 from Monday. Our impression is that speculative players, whose increased involvement in palladium has been notable of late, were largely responsible for palladium’s outperformance. Investors that had begun the week short palladium were doubtless driven to cover after prices held above $630 on Monday and into Tuesday. In addition, an accumulation of option interest at key levels helped maintain buying above $660. - The first week in December saw speculative futures positions increase by more than 80,000 ounces. Much of this is likely to have been short covering—a development we predicted given that the previous week’s shortening was followed by a sudden and unexpected price hike. - Palladium ETFs on the whole were net liquidators last week, shedding 12,000 ounces of physical holdings. This is small compared with the previous week’s selling of 54,000 ounces, however— unsurprising given the week’s positive price action. Expect palladium ETFs to turn net buyers this week if the spot price continues to outperform the other precious metals. #### **Palladium Exchange Investment, Apr 09—December 11** 2,000 1,000
